from sqlalchemy.orm import Session
from sqlalchemy import or_
from typing import Optional, List
from datetime import datetime

from ..models.user import (
    User, UserProfile, UserAddress, UserEmergencyContact,
    UserNotificationSetting,
)
from ..schemas.user import (
    UserDetailResponse, UserProfileResponse, UserProfileUpdateRequest,
    UserAddressResponse, UserAddressCreateRequest,
    EmergencyContactResponse, EmergencyContactCreateRequest,
    NotificationSettingsResponse, NotificationSettingsUpdateRequest,
    UserUpdateRequest,
)
from ..schemas.auth import UserBasicResponse
from ..schemas.common import PaginatedMeta
from ..core.exceptions import NotFoundException, BadRequestException


class UserService:
    """Handles all user CRUD operations."""

    def __init__(self, db: Session):
        self.db = db

    # ============================================
    # GET USER BY ID
    # ============================================
    def get_user_by_id(self, user_id: str) -> Optional[User]:
        return self.db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).first()

    # ============================================
    # GET USER BY EMAIL
    # ============================================
    def get_user_by_email(self, email: str) -> Optional[User]:
        return self.db.query(User).filter(User.email == email).first()

    # ============================================
    # GET USER DETAIL (full profile)
    # ============================================
    def get_user_detail(self, user_id: str) -> UserDetailResponse:
        user = self.get_user_by_id(user_id)
        if not user:
            raise NotFoundException("User not found")

        profile = self.db.query(UserProfile).filter(UserProfile.user_id == user_id).first()
        addresses = self.db.query(UserAddress).filter(UserAddress.user_id == user_id).all()
        emergency_contacts = self.db.query(UserEmergencyContact).filter(UserEmergencyContact.user_id == user_id).all()
        notif_settings = self.db.query(UserNotificationSetting).filter(UserNotificationSetting.user_id == user_id).first()

        # Get roles
        from ..models.user import UserRole, Role
        role_rows = (
            self.db.query(Role.name)
            .join(UserRole, UserRole.role_id == Role.id)
            .filter(UserRole.user_id == user_id, UserRole.is_active == True)
            .all()
        )
        roles = [r[0] for r in role_rows]
        primary_role = "client"
        if user.primary_role_id:
            role = self.db.query(Role).filter(Role.id == user.primary_role_id).first()
            if role:
                primary_role = role.name

        return UserDetailResponse(
            id=user.id,
            email=user.email,
            full_name=user.full_name,
            phone=user.phone,
            gender=user.gender,
            date_of_birth=user.date_of_birth,
            profile_image=user.profile_image,
            blood_group=user.blood_group,
            primary_role=primary_role,
            roles=roles,
            is_verified=user.is_verified,
            is_admin_approved=user.is_admin_approved,
            is_active=user.is_active,
            is_online=user.is_online,
            profile=UserProfileResponse.model_validate(profile) if profile else None,
            addresses=[UserAddressResponse.model_validate(a) for a in addresses],
            emergency_contacts=[EmergencyContactResponse.model_validate(ec) for ec in emergency_contacts],
            notification_settings=NotificationSettingsResponse.model_validate(notif_settings) if notif_settings else None,
            created_at=user.created_at,
            updated_at=user.updated_at,
        )

    # ============================================
    # UPDATE USER
    # ============================================
    def update_user(self, user_id: str, data: UserUpdateRequest) -> User:
        user = self.get_user_by_id(user_id)
        if not user:
            raise NotFoundException("User not found")

        update_fields = data.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
        for field, value in update_fields.items():
            setattr(user, field, value)

        self.db.commit()
        self.db.refresh(user)
        return user

    # ============================================
    # UPDATE USER PROFILE
    # ============================================
    def update_profile(self, user_id: str, data: UserProfileUpdateRequest) -> UserProfile:
        profile = self.db.query(UserProfile).filter(UserProfile.user_id == user_id).first()
        if not profile:
            raise NotFoundException("User profile not found")

        update_fields = data.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
        for field, value in update_fields.items():
            setattr(profile, field, value)

        self.db.commit()
        self.db.refresh(profile)
        return profile

    # ============================================
    # ADDRESSES
    # ============================================
    def add_address(self, user_id: str, data: UserAddressCreateRequest) -> UserAddress:
        if data.is_primary:
            self.db.query(UserAddress).filter(
                UserAddress.user_id == user_id, UserAddress.is_primary == True
            ).update({"is_primary": False})

        address = UserAddress(user_id=user_id, **data.model_dump())
        self.db.add(address)
        self.db.commit()
        self.db.refresh(address)
        return address

    def get_addresses(self, user_id: str) -> List[UserAddress]:
        return self.db.query(UserAddress).filter(UserAddress.user_id == user_id).all()

    def delete_address(self, user_id: str, address_id: str) -> None:
        address = self.db.query(UserAddress).filter(
            UserAddress.id == address_id, UserAddress.user_id == user_id
        ).first()
        if not address:
            raise NotFoundException("Address not found")
        self.db.delete(address)
        self.db.commit()

    # ============================================
    # EMERGENCY CONTACTS
    # ============================================
    def add_emergency_contact(self, user_id: str, data: EmergencyContactCreateRequest) -> UserEmergencyContact:
        if data.is_primary:
            self.db.query(UserEmergencyContact).filter(
                UserEmergencyContact.user_id == user_id, UserEmergencyContact.is_primary == True
            ).update({"is_primary": False})

        contact = UserEmergencyContact(user_id=user_id, **data.model_dump())
        self.db.add(contact)
        self.db.commit()
        self.db.refresh(contact)
        return contact

    def get_emergency_contacts(self, user_id: str) -> List[UserEmergencyContact]:
        return self.db.query(UserEmergencyContact).filter(UserEmergencyContact.user_id == user_id).all()

    def delete_emergency_contact(self, user_id: str, contact_id: str) -> None:
        contact = self.db.query(UserEmergencyContact).filter(
            UserEmergencyContact.id == contact_id, UserEmergencyContact.user_id == user_id
        ).first()
        if not contact:
            raise NotFoundException("Emergency contact not found")
        self.db.delete(contact)
        self.db.commit()

    # ============================================
    # NOTIFICATION SETTINGS
    # ============================================
    def get_notification_settings(self, user_id: str) -> UserNotificationSetting:
        settings = self.db.query(UserNotificationSetting).filter(
            UserNotificationSetting.user_id == user_id
        ).first()
        if not settings:
            # Create default settings
            settings = UserNotificationSetting(user_id=user_id)
            self.db.add(settings)
            self.db.commit()
            self.db.refresh(settings)
        return settings

    def update_notification_settings(self, user_id: str, data: NotificationSettingsUpdateRequest) -> UserNotificationSetting:
        settings = self.get_notification_settings(user_id)
        update_fields = data.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
        for field, value in update_fields.items():
            setattr(settings, field, value)
        self.db.commit()
        self.db.refresh(settings)
        return settings

    # ============================================
    # LIST USERS (Admin)
    # ============================================
    def list_users(
        self, page: int = 1, size: int = 20, search: Optional[str] = None, role: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> dict:
        query = self.db.query(User)

        if search:
            search_term = f"%{search}%"
            query = query.filter(
                or_(
                    User.full_name.ilike(search_term),
                    User.email.ilike(search_term),
                    User.phone.ilike(search_term),
                )
            )

        if role:
            from ..models.user import UserRole, Role
            query = query.join(UserRole, UserRole.user_id == User.id).join(
                Role, Role.id == UserRole.role_id
            ).filter(Role.name == role)

        total = query.count()
        users = query.offset((page - 1) * size).limit(size).all()

        return {
            "items": users,
            "total": total,
            "page": page,
            "size": size,
            "pages": (total + size - 1) // size if size > 0 else 0,
        }

    # ============================================
    # DEACTIVATE USER
    # ============================================
    def deactivate_user(self, user_id: str) -> None:
        user = self.get_user_by_id(user_id)
        if not user:
            raise NotFoundException("User not found")
        user.is_active = False
        self.db.commit()

    def activate_user(self, user_id: str) -> None:
        user = self.get_user_by_id(user_id)
        if not user:
            raise NotFoundException("User not found")
        user.is_active = True
        self.db.commit()

    return app

from mysql.connector import pooling
from .config import Config

_connection_pool = None

def get_connection_pool():
    """Initialize MySQL connection pool"""
    global _connection_pool
    if _connection_pool is None:
        _connection_pool = pooling.MySQLConnectionPool(
            pool_name="aetherion_pool",
            pool_size=10,
            pool_reset_session=True,
            host=Config.DB_HOST,
            port=Config.DB_PORT,
            user=Config.DB_USER,
            password=Config.DB_PASSWORD,
            database=Config.DB_NAME,
            charset='utf8mb4',
            collation='utf8mb4_unicode_ci',
        )

class DB:
    """Database helper class for executing queries"""
    
    @staticmethod
    def fetch_one(sql, params=None):

        db = get_db()
        cursor = db.cursor(dictionary=True)
        try:
            cursor.execute(sql, params or ())
            result = cursor.fetchone()
            return result
        finally:
            cursor.close()
            db.close()
    
    @staticmethod
    def fetch_all(sql, params=None):
        """Fetch all rows as list of dicts"""
        db = get_db()
        cursor = db.cursor(dictionary=True)
        try:

            result = cursor.fetchall()

        finally:
            cursor.close()

    @staticmethod
    def execute(sql, params=None):
        """Execute a write query and return lastrowid"""
        db = get_db()
        cursor = db.cursor()
        try:
            cursor.execute(sql, params or ())
            db.commit()
            return cursor.lastrowid
        except Exception as e:
            db.rollback()
            raise e
        finally:
            cursor.close()
            db.close()
    
    @staticmethod
    def execute_many(sql, params_list):
        """Execute many rows at once"""
        db = get_db()

        try:
            cursor.executemany(sql, params_list)

        except Exception as e:

## 2. Core Layer (app/core/)

- **constants.py**: 30+ Enum classes — `UserRole` (13 roles from super_admin to normal_user), `AppointmentType`, `AppointmentStatus`, `AppointmentLocation`, `AppointmentPriority`, `DoctorStatus`, `HospitalType`, `BedType`, `MedicineCategory`, `MedicineForm`, `OrderStatus`, `PaymentMethod`, `PaymentStatus`, `EmergencyServiceType`, `EmergencyPriority`, `BloodGroup`, `DonationType`, `PregnancyTrimester`, `PregnancyStatus`, `ReviewableType`, `MessageType`, `NotificationPriority`, `AIMessageRole`, `AIEmotion`, `OxygenStockStatus`, and more.
- **exceptions.py**: `AppException(HTTPException)` base, plus `NotFoundException(404)`, `UnauthorizedException(401)`, `ForbiddenException(403)`, `ConflictException(409)`, `BadRequestException(400)`, `ValidationException(422)`, `RateLimitException(429)`, `InternalServerException(500)`.
- **permissions.py**: `CurrentUser` dataclass (id, email, full_name, role, roles, primary_role, is_active, is_admin_approved, is_verified) with helper properties (is_admin, is_doctor, is_patient, etc.). RBAC functions: `require_role(*roles)`, `require_admin()`, `require_doctor()`, `require_patient()`, `require_hospital()`, `require_pharmacy()`, `require_verified()`, `require_approved()`.

## 3. Application Structure

- **main.py**: FastAPI app with `lifespan` handler (verifies DB connection on startup), CORS middleware, HTTP request logging middleware. App factory pattern. Root `/` returns name/version/status. `/health` returns DB connectivity health.
- **routers registered in `api/v1/__init__.py`**: 15 routers under `api_v1_prefix="/api/v1"`. Each router is included as a module.

## 4. Authentication/JWT

- **Config**: JWT_SECRET_KEY, JWT_ALGORITHM (HS256), ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES (15), REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS (7) in config.py (loaded from .env).
- **security.py**: `hash_password()` (bcrypt via passlib), `verify_password()`, `create_access_token()` (data + optional expires_delta, sets type="access"), `create_refresh_token()` (data + type="refresh"), `decode_token()` (returns None on JWTError).
- **auth_middleware.py**: `get_current_user()` — extracts Bearer token, decodes JWT, queries `users` table by `sub`, loads roles from `user_roles` + `roles` tables, returns `CurrentUser`. `get_current_user_optional()` — same but returns None if no token.
- **auth_service.py**: `AuthService(db)` — full implementations for login (verify password, load roles, create tokens, store session), register (validate, hash, insert user + profile + role), refresh_token (verify session, create new access), logout (revoke sessions), forgot/reset/change password, verify_email.
- **Token structure**: `{"sub": user_id, "role": primary_role, "roles": list, "type": "access"/"refresh", "exp": ...}`

## 5. Database Session Management

- **database.py**: SQLAlchemy `create_engine` with MySQL+pymysql URL, pool_size=20, pool_pre_ping=True. `SessionLocal = sessionmaker()`. `Base = declarative_base()`. `get_db()` generator yield/close pattern for FastAPI Depends.
- **Base model**: `base.py` defines `BaseModel` mixin with UUID `id` (CHAR(36) primary key), `created_at`, `updated_at` with server defaults.

## 6. Error Handling

- Custom exception hierarchy extends `HTTPException`. Services raise exceptions like `NotFoundException`, `UnauthorizedException`, `ConflictException`.
- No global exception handler middleware registered in main.py yet (FastAPI handles HTTPException subclasses natively).

## 7. Logging

- **main.py**: `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)` with `logger = logging.getLogger("aetherion")`.
- HTTP request logging middleware logs method, path, status code, duration for all API requests.

## 8. Models Directory

17 model files covering ~55+ ORM models (detailed above). All models extend `Base` (SQLAlchemy declarative base) and `BaseModel` (UUID PK mixin). Uses `sqlalchemy.dialects.mysql.CHAR` for UUID FKs. Heavy use of `SQLEnum`, `JSON`, `DECIMAL`, `ForeignKey`, `Index` with `__table_args__`.

## 9. Services Directory

15 service files, each with a class (e.g., `AuthService`, `UserService`, `DoctorService`). Constructor takes `db: Session`. Methods are either sync or async. Core services (auth, user) are fully implemented with real DB queries. Others are stubs/placeholder classes.

## 10. Schemas Directory

15 schemas files + common.py. Uses Pydantic v2 with `BaseModel`, `EmailStr`, `Field(...)`, `model_config = {"from_attributes": True}`. Common schemas include `APIResponse`, `PaginatedResponse`, `PaginationParams`, `PaginatedMeta`, `HealthCheckResponse`. Each domain has request/response schemas.

## 11. API Routes (api/v1/)

15 route files. Pattern: `router = APIRouter(prefix="/module", tags=["Module"])`. Uses `Depends(get_db)` for sessions, `Depends(get_current_user)` for auth, `Depends(require_admin())` for RBAC. Response pattern: `return APIResponse(success=True, message="...", data=...)`.

## 12. Dependencies

**requirements.txt**: fastapi 0.115.0, uvicorn 0.30.6, sqlalchemy 2.0.35, pymysql 1.1.1, alembic 1.13.2, python-jose[cryptography] 3.3.0, passlib[bcrypt] 1.7.4, python-multipart 0.0.9, pydantic 2.9.2, pydantic-settings 2.5.2, fastapi-mail 1.4.2, python-dotenv 1.0.1, redis 5.1.1, pytest 8.3.3, httpx 0.27.2.

## 13. Tests

Only 2 existing tests in `tests/test_auth.py` — test_root and test_health. Conftest uses TestClient from FastAPI.

## 14. Docker

- **Dockerfile**: python:3.11-slim, pip install from requirements.txt, CMD uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
- **docker-compose.yml**: mysql:8.0, redis:7-alpine, api service (build: ., port 8000). Named volume for MySQL data.

## Key Architectural Notes

- **Two backends exist**: FastAPI (`app/`) is the primary/target. Flask (`app2/` + `flask_app.py`) is legacy. The architecture analysis doc explicitly targets FastAPI as the implementation path.
- **Auth system IS fully real/working** — the analysis doc describes the old stub state, but the actual files now contain real DB-backed implementations.
- **The architecture analysis doc** (`ARCHITECTURE_ANALYSIS.md`) is an essential reference — 2411 lines detailing every missing endpoint, FK type mismatch, and implementation priority across 16 modules.
- **The SQL schema** has 85 tables with 8 views, 6 stored procedures, 8 triggers, 180+ indexes — only ~55 have ORM models currently.
args.next_steps: The main takeaway is that the FastAPI backend has a solid foundation (config, database, core exceptions/permissions, auth with real DB queries, JWT utilities) but only auth and user modules are fully implemented. The architecture analysis doc provides a detailed phased implementation plan for the remaining 14+ modules totaling ~197 endpoints. Next steps would be to pick a module from Phase 2 (Doctor, Hospital, Pharmacy, Appointment, Patient) and implement schemas → service → routes for that module.

## 2. Core Layer (app/core/)

- **constants.py**: 30+ Enum classes — `UserRole` (13 roles from super_admin to normal_user), `AppointmentType`, `AppointmentStatus`, `AppointmentLocation`, `AppointmentPriority`, `DoctorStatus`, `HospitalType`, `BedType`, `MedicineCategory`, `MedicineForm`, `OrderStatus`, `PaymentMethod`, `PaymentStatus`, `EmergencyServiceType`, `EmergencyPriority`, `BloodGroup`, `DonationType`, `PregnancyTrimester`, `PregnancyStatus`, `ReviewableType`, `MessageType`, `NotificationPriority`, `AIMessageRole`, `AIEmotion`, `OxygenStockStatus`, and more.
- **exceptions.py**: `AppException(HTTPException)` base, plus `NotFoundException(404)`, `UnauthorizedException(401)`, `ForbiddenException(403)`, `ConflictException(409)`, `BadRequestException(400)`, `ValidationException(422)`, `RateLimitException(429)`, `InternalServerException(500)`.
- **permissions.py**: `CurrentUser` dataclass (id, email, full_name, role, roles, primary_role, is_active, is_admin_approved, is_verified) with helper properties (is_admin, is_doctor, is_patient, etc.). RBAC functions: `require_role(*roles)`, `require_admin()`, `require_doctor()`, `require_patient()`, `require_hospital()`, `require_pharmacy()`, `require_verified()`, `require_approved()`.

## 3. Application Structure

- **main.py**: FastAPI app with `lifespan` handler (verifies DB connection on startup), CORS middleware, HTTP request logging middleware. App factory pattern. Root `/` returns name/version/status. `/health` returns DB connectivity health.
- **routers registered in `api/v1/__init__.py`**: 15 routers under `api_v1_prefix="/api/v1"`. Each router is included as a module.

## 4. Authentication/JWT

- **Config**: JWT_SECRET_KEY, JWT_ALGORITHM (HS256), ACCESS_TOKEN_EXPIRE_MINUTES (15), REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRE_DAYS (7) in config.py (loaded from .env).
- **security.py**: `hash_password()` (bcrypt via passlib), `verify_password()`, `create_access_token()` (data + optional expires_delta, sets type="access"), `create_refresh_token()` (data + type="refresh"), `decode_token()` (returns None on JWTError).
- **auth_middleware.py**: `get_current_user()` — extracts Bearer token, decodes JWT, queries `users` table by `sub`, loads roles from `user_roles` + `roles` tables, returns `CurrentUser`. `get_current_user_optional()` — same but returns None if no token.
- **auth_service.py**: `AuthService(db)` — full implementations for login (verify password, load roles, create tokens, store session), register (validate, hash, insert user + profile + role), refresh_token (verify session, create new access), logout (revoke sessions), forgot/reset/change password, verify_email.
- **Token structure**: `{"sub": user_id, "role": primary_role, "roles": list, "type": "access"/"refresh", "exp": ...}`

## 5. Database Session Management

- **database.py**: SQLAlchemy `create_engine` with MySQL+pymysql URL, pool_size=20, pool_pre_ping=True. `SessionLocal = sessionmaker()`. `Base = declarative_base()`. `get_db()` generator yield/close pattern for FastAPI Depends.
- **Base model**: `base.py` defines `BaseModel` mixin with UUID `id` (CHAR(36) primary key), `created_at`, `updated_at` with server defaults.

## 6. Error Handling

- Custom exception hierarchy extends `HTTPException`. Services raise exceptions like `NotFoundException`, `UnauthorizedException`, `ConflictException`.
- No global exception handler middleware registered in main.py yet (FastAPI handles HTTPException subclasses natively).

## 7. Logging

- **main.py**: `logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)` with `logger = logging.getLogger("aetherion")`.
- HTTP request logging middleware logs method, path, status code, duration for all API requests.

## 8. Models Directory

17 model files covering ~55+ ORM models (detailed above). All models extend `Base` (SQLAlchemy declarative base) and `BaseModel` (UUID PK mixin). Uses `sqlalchemy.dialects.mysql.CHAR` for UUID FKs. Heavy use of `SQLEnum`, `JSON`, `DECIMAL`, `ForeignKey`, `Index` with `__table_args__`.

## 9. Services Directory

15 service files, each with a class (e.g., `AuthService`, `UserService`, `DoctorService`). Constructor takes `db: Session`. Methods are either sync or async. Core services (auth, user) are fully implemented with real DB queries. Others are stubs/placeholder classes.

## 10. Schemas Directory

15 schemas files + common.py. Uses Pydantic v2 with `BaseModel`, `EmailStr`, `Field(...)`, `model_config = {"from_attributes": True}`. Common schemas include `APIResponse`, `PaginatedResponse`, `PaginationParams`, `PaginatedMeta`, `HealthCheckResponse`. Each domain has request/response schemas.

## 11. API Routes (api/v1/)

15 route files. Pattern: `router = APIRouter(prefix="/module", tags=["Module"])`. Uses `Depends(get_db)` for sessions, `Depends(get_current_user)` for auth, `Depends(require_admin())` for RBAC. Response pattern: `return APIResponse(success=True, message="...", data=...)`.

## 12. Dependencies

**requirements.txt**: fastapi 0.115.0, uvicorn 0.30.6, sqlalchemy 2.0.35, pymysql 1.1.1, alembic 1.13.2, python-jose[cryptography] 3.3.0, passlib[bcrypt] 1.7.4, python-multipart 0.0.9, pydantic 2.9.2, pydantic-settings 2.5.2, fastapi-mail 1.4.2, python-dotenv 1.0.1, redis 5.1.1, pytest 8.3.3, httpx 0.27.2.

## 13. Tests

Only 2 existing tests in `tests/test_auth.py` — test_root and test_health. Conftest uses TestClient from FastAPI.

## 14. Docker

- **Dockerfile**: python:3.11-slim, pip install from requirements.txt, CMD uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
- **docker-compose.yml**: mysql:8.0, redis:7-alpine, api service (build: ., port 8000). Named volume for MySQL data.

- **Two backends exist**: FastAPI (`app/`) is the primary/target. Flask (`app2/` + `flask_app.py`) is legacy. The architecture analysis doc explicitly targets FastAPI as the implementation path.
- **Auth system IS fully real/working** — the analysis doc describes the old stub state, but the actual files now contain real DB-backed implementations.
- **The architecture analysis doc** (`ARCHITECTURE_ANALYSIS.md`) is an essential reference — 2411 lines detailing every missing endpoint, FK type mismatch, and implementation priority across 16 modules.
- **The SQL schema** has 85 tables with 8 views, 6 stored procedures, 8 triggers, 180+ indexes — only ~55 have ORM models currently.

functionDeclarations.name: glob
functionDeclarations.description: Efficiently finds files matching specific glob patterns (e.g., `src/**/*.ts`, `**/*.md`), returning absolute paths sorted by modification time (newest first). Ideal for quickly locating files based on their name or path structure, especially in large codebases.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match against (e.g., '**/*.py', 'docs/*.md').

path.description: Optional: The absolute path to the directory to search within. If omitted, searches the root directory.

case_sensitive.description: Optional: Whether the search should be case-sensitive. Defaults to false.

respect_git_ignore.description: Optional: Whether to respect .gitignore patterns when finding files. Only available in git repositories. Defaults to true.

maxResults.description: Optional: Maximum number of file paths to return (default: 1000). Use to limit output for broad patterns.

functionDeclarations.name: list_directory
functionDeclarations.description: Lists the names of files and subdirectories directly within a specified directory path. Can optionally ignore entries matching provided glob patterns.

path.description: The absolute path to the directory to list (must be absolute, not relative)

ignore.description: List of glob patterns to ignore

file_filtering_options.description: Optional: Whether to respect ignore patterns from .gitignore or .geminiignore

respect_git_ignore.description: Optional: Whether to respect .gitignore patterns when listing files. Only available in git repositories. Defaults to true.

respect_gemini_ignore.description: Optional: Whether to respect .geminiignore patterns when listing files. Defaults to true.

functionDeclarations.name: read_file
functionDeclarations.description: Reads and returns the content of a specified file. By default reads up to 2000 lines starting from the beginning of the file. Files whose selected range exceeds 256 KB are truncated with an advisory; use 'offset' and 'limit' only if the file is too large to read at once — it's recommended to read the whole file by not providing these parameters. Handles text, images (PNG, JPG, GIF, WEBP, SVG, BMP), and PDF files. For images, videos or other multimedia files, use the 'analyze_multimedia' tool if available.

absolute_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read (e.g., '/home/user/project/file.txt'). Relative paths are not supported. You must provide an absolute path.

offset.description: Optional: For text files, the 0-based line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

limit.description: Optional: For text files, the maximum number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

functionDeclarations.name: run_shell_command
functionDeclarations.description:
This tool executes a given shell command using the best available Windows shell (PowerShell Core, Windows PowerShell, or Command Prompt).

IMPORTANT:
- This tool is for terminal operations (e.g., git / npm / docker / build & test commands).
- DO NOT use this tool for file operations like reading, writing, editing, or searching files. Prefer the dedicated file tools for those actions.
- Quote any file path that contains spaces with double quotes, e.g. `cd "/path with spaces"` or `python "/path with spaces/script.py"`.
- If a command would produce very large output, prefer adding flags/filters (narrow paths, limit counts, request specific fields, machine-readable formats like JSON) to keep output small and unambiguous.
- Very large outputs may be returned as the most recent tail of the output. Earlier content may be truncated from the beginning. If the tool reports a "Full output saved to: <path>", that file contains the full command output. Use the exact path returned by the tool, then prefer searching that file first (grep/rg or platform equivalents) for specific ERROR/WARN/FAIL/SUCCESS markers, then reading small slices (with `read_file` using `offset`/`limit`) or tailing the log file instead of re-running expensive commands.
- Do not append truncating pipelines such as `| tail`, `| Select-Object -Last`, or similar to an expensive first run just to suppress output. Those discard earlier context and force a re-run if you later need omitted lines. Let the tool/log capture the full output, then inspect the saved log file.
- When issuing multiple shell commands in one response, parallelize only when they are truly independent and do not compete for the same files, directories, logs, locks, caches, git state, or ports. If one command depends on another or shared state may race, run them sequentially.

The following information is returned:
- Command: Executed command.
- Directory: Directory where command was executed, or `(root)`.
- Output: Combined command output (stdout/stderr). Can be `(empty)` or an excerpt if very large.
- Error: Error or `(none)` if no error was reported for the subprocess.
- Exit Code: Exit code or `(none)` if terminated by signal.
- Signal: Signal number or `(none)` if no signal was received.

command.description: Exact command to execute using the best available Windows shell (automatically selected from PowerShell Core, Windows PowerShell, or Command Prompt). Quote any file paths containing spaces with double quotes.

description.description: Brief description of the command for the user. Be specific and concise. Ideally a single sentence. Can be up to 3 sentences for clarity. No line breaks.

directory.description: (OPTIONAL) The absolute path of the directory to run the command in. If not provided, the project root directory is used. Must be a directory within the workspace and must already exist.

run_in_background.description: Set to true to run this command in the background. Returns immediately with task metadata and an output file path.

functionDeclarations.name: search_file_content
functionDeclarations.description: Searches for a regular expression pattern within the content of files in a specified directory, a specific file, or the current working directory. Can filter files by a glob pattern when searching directories. Returns the lines containing matches, along with their file paths and line numbers.

pattern.description: The regular expression (regex) pattern to search for within file contents (e.g., 'function\s+myFunction', 'import\s+\{.*\}\s+from\s+.*').

path.description: Optional: The absolute path to a directory or file to search within. If a file path is provided, searches only within that file. If a directory path is provided, searches all files in that directory. If omitted, searches the current working directory.

include.description: Optional: A glob pattern to filter which files are searched (e.g., '*.js', '*.{ts,tsx}', 'src/**'). Only applicable when searching directories, ignored for file searches. If omitted, searches all files (respecting potential global ignores).

maxResults.description: Optional: Maximum number of matches to return to prevent context overflow (default: 20, max: 150). Values above 150 are clamped automatically. Use lower values for broad searches, higher for specific searches.
